phase3_findings.description: $failed_present is a coarse OR across two non-equivalent channels. `((($failed_raw|type)=="array") or (($assess_raw|type)=="array"))` becomes true when EITHER phase3_failed_agents or shadow.per_reviewer_assessment is a well-formed array, but the primary phase3_failed_agents sink covers ALL dispatched Phase-3 agents while the shadow assessment covers only the shadow subset. On an agent-mutable/hand-corrupted workpad where phase3_failed_agents is malformed (object / false / scalar) yet shadow.per_reviewer_assessment is a well-formed array, $failed_present=true, so a general Phase-3 agent that is dispatched, absent from findings, and not in the shadow set resolves to `silent` (agent_disposition falls past the failed_present!not guard) even though the authoritative sink establishing its failed-vs-silent status was malformed/unestablished. This is exactly the 'collapse an unestablished failed-set onto silent' residual the change exists to prevent, and the in-code comment ('a silent agent under a malformed failed field reads unestablished, never silent') is over-broad for the mixed-channel case.

Three adversarial phase3_failed_agents shapes (iter-4 `0` numeric-falsy, iter-5 `""` empty-string, iter-6 `7` scalar-number) are constructed and fed through but only aggregate facts (exit 0, .iterations==6) are asserted — the per-agent disposition of silent agent `z` is asserted only for the `{}`, `"z"`, and `false` shapes. The issue's AC requires each adversarial shape to 'land in a specific arm'; a future change coercing a numeric-falsy/empty-string/scalar failed field to an empty array (establishing 'no failures') would silently map `z` to silent and these three iters would stay green.

The shadow-channel-only failed-set path (phase3_failed_agents absent, $failed_present established solely via shadow per_reviewer_assessment) is never exercised with a third dispatched-silent agent, so the 'shadow establishes failed_present → silent (not unestablished)' branch is untested; iter-4's roster is only [a returned, f failed].

Malformed shadow.per_reviewer_assessment (a second agent-mutable producer value feeding the failed set) has no adversarial coverage: non-array shapes and entries missing .agent or with a non-boolean .returned are never asserted to (a) not abort the filter and (b) contribute no spurious failed entries.

The 'adds no new verdict, perturbs no derivation' claim is verdict-asserted only for the null case (deferred-only agent b). No assertion pins the verdict of a returning findings-bearing agent, even though the diff rewired verdict_for to the new $af binding — a regression on the findings path would be uncaught.

fix_decisions roll-up (map(.fix_decision)|map(strings)|unique) is asserted only for single-value ['deferred'] and empty [] sets; the sort-unique of a multi/duplicate set and the strings type-guard dropping a non-string element have no witness.

The top-of-file 'Narrowed null class' / 'Denominator confound' block (lib/efficiency-trace.jq lines 55-71) is design/analysis narrative that restates docs/internal/efficiency-trace.md's Denominator-confound section; it names no specific wrong edit it prevents at that source location and runs well over three physical lines, so it fails the prevention-only comment standard for library-source comments. Belongs in the internal doc where it already exists.

Pre-existing (NOT introduced by this PR): def finding_agent (.agent) and the new fix_decisions map(.fix_decision) index unguarded on agent-mutable phase3_findings elements, so a scalar element aborts the whole filter — but the pre-existing roster-construction line aborts first on the same input, so the PR changes no observable failure. Noted for the hardening focus area only; finding_kind demonstrates the guarded pattern finding_agent lacks.
